text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Wednesday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Latvian Prime Minister Andris Shkele said after a press conference in Copenhagen that Latvia intends to take Lithuania to an international court over their disputed territory in the Baltic sea.
- A court began reading the indictment to the plotters of the coup and crackdown on January 13, 1991 when 13 people were killed.
- Official reserves of the central bank, the Bank of Lithuania, increased by $6.9 million, or 0.8 percent in October, and were estimated at $842.8 million.

- Lietuvos Gelezinkeliai (Lithuanian Railroad Company) started to make a profit in October. It transported a record three million tons of cargo and boosted its activity by 43 percent when compared with the same period last year.
- Polish Kredyt Bank opens its first branch office outside Poland and becomes the first foreign bank in Lithuania. It is expected to start operations in April 1997.

- Some 20,000 shares worth 158 litas each of the Klaipedos Nafta oil terminal were sold on the stock exchange on Tuesday. The whole deal was worth 3.2 million litas. According to unconfirmed information, the shares were bought by Russian oil companies LUKoil and Jukos.

- The Lithuanian Centre Union, the third biggest party in the new parliament, declared that they will support Gediminas Vagnorius for the post of new prime minister if President Algirdas Brazauskas nominates him.

- The left-wing Social Democrats, who have 12 seats in the new parliament, will remain in "constructive opposition" but will not unite their efforts with the Lithuanian Democratic Labour Party (LDLP), ousted from power in the elections.

- The prime ministers of Scandinavian countries in Copenhagen at a meeting of the Nordic Council declared clearly that they are ready to support the aims of the Baltic countries to join NATO and the European Union (EU).

- The Vilnius Prosecutor's office said that according to its evidence the main cause of the December 1995 bank crisis was the central bank, which failed to carry out its duties properly. A criminal case will be started against the former leaders of the central bank, prosecutors said.
